analysis: Uniform transition weighting did not improve validation: macro HR@10 was 0.4975, versus 0.500 for the preceding exponential-weight trial and the reported 0.505 baseline. Category HR@10: Movies_and_TV 0.585, Industrial_and_Scientific 0.530, Electronics 0.400, CDs_and_Vinyl 0.475. This result does not support the proposed benefit of uniform weighting; it does not establish why performance declined. The trial completed successfully using 528.21 allocated GPU-seconds. No test metrics were used.
code_summary: Trained one independent SASRec model per category: 96-dimensional embeddings, two causal Transformer blocks, two attention heads, dropout 0.2, cosine scoring with jointly learned item bias and scale. The isolated change assigns uniform weights to up to 24 randomly selected valid transitions per history, preserving per-history loss normalization. Training retains 256 sampled negatives with exclusion masks, prefix augmentation, AdamW, cosine learning-rate decay, seed 42, and validation-based single-checkpoint selection. Prediction routes each category to exactly one checkpoint; no ensembles or separately fitted scoring components.
